Actor.description: `[[actors]]` — one named worker in the project.

name.description:
Unique actor name; the value an `assignee:` field (or a
`[tasks.assignee] allowed` entry) references.

roles.description: Roles the actor holds, each naming a declared `[[roles]]` entry.

oneOf.description: A person.
A language model.

comments.description:
Whether the scaffold carries explanatory `#` comments — the header block
and the per-slot annotations (kind, required/optional, choices, default).
`true` (default) keeps them; `false` strips every comment, leaving a bare
mapping of slot names to values.

editor.description:
Editor command override. Falls back to `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, then a
built-in default. May carry arguments (split on whitespace).

header.description:
Scaffold header override. Absent uses the built-in instructions; an empty
(or all-blank) string disables the header; any other text replaces it,
comment-prefixed so it stays valid YAML. Ignored when `comments = false`.

Anchor.description: One labelled point in an anchor classification.

color.description: Optional colour: a named ANSI colour or `#RRGGBB`.

value.description: The point on the scale this label names.

AssigneeConfig.description: `[tasks.assignee]` — who may be named, and whether one must be.

allowed.description: Allowed assignees (the project's actors). Empty = accept any value.

required.description: Whether an assignee must be set.

Band.description: One contiguous labelled range in a band classification.

color.description: Optional colour: a named ANSI colour or `#RRGGBB`.

max.description: Upper bound (inclusive for int and the last real band; else exclusive).

Category.description: One categorical bucket: a predicate plus its representative score and display.

color.description: Optional colour: a named ANSI colour or `#RRGGBB`.

label.description: Display label; falls back to empty when absent.

score.description: Representative score on the scale (drives banding and sort).

when.description: evalexpr predicate over the inputs selecting this category.

CheckSpec.description:
`check = { typst, function, field }` — a `[[tasks.rules]]` entry that
delegates to a Typst function instead of a filter expression. See
[`crate::config_rules_typst`] for the evaluation route.

field.description:
Field whose value the function receives (`none` when the task omits
it). Absent means the function receives the whole task, in the shape
`mt eval --json` prints.

function.description: Name of the function `typst` exports that this rule calls.

typst.description:
Path to the Typst module exporting `function`, relative to the project
root (the directory holding `.mindtape/`).

oneOf.description: Each folder name as an independent flat tag (`backend`, `auth`).

Cumulative path prefixes joined by the separator (`backend`,
`backend:auth`).

when.description:
Whether this column renders, as a condition expression — the same
grammar `[[ls.rules]]` uses (`tty()`, `format()`, `env()`,
`on_branch()`, `now()`, `weekday()`, `true` / `false`), plus the four
listing predicates only a column resolution can answer: `nonempty()`,
`contested()`, `named()`, `blocked()`.

Absent means the column never renders. The embedded floor carries one
per column, so an absent `when` is a column the project deleted from
the floor rather than a column awaiting a built-in default.

CommentsConfig.description: `[tasks.comments]` — review-comment policy over a task's whole source file.

allow-pattern.description:
Regex permitting a deliberate comment form — matched against the
comment's stripped, trimmed inner text — even under `warn`/`forbid`.

policy.description: Whether a comment is unconstrained, reported, or fails `mt check`.

CommentsPolicy.description: How `mt check` treats a comment found in a task's source.

oneOf.description: Comments are unconstrained. The default.
A comment is reported but `mt check` still succeeds.
A comment is reported and fails `mt check`.

ContentAssert.description: The assertion made over a matched section's content: the string `"non-empty"`, or a one-key table `{ min-words = N }`, `{ max-words = N }`, `{ must-match = "regex" }`, `{ must-not-match = "regex" }`, or `{ density = { pattern = "regex", max = N, per = "section" } }`.

min-words.description: The section must contain at least this many words.

max-words.description: The section must contain at most this many words.

must-match.description: Rust regex the section's source text must match.

must-not-match.description: Rust regex the section's source text must not match.

rules.description: Ordered list of section-content gating rules.

ContentRuleConfig.description:
One entry in `[[tasks.body.content.rules]]`.

`path` selects the section(s) — the heading tree paths the header rules
already use — and `assert` is the assertion made over each matched
section's content. Like every header rule, it carries the optional `when`
filter and `message` override.

assert.description: The assertion made over each matched section's content.

message.description: Override for the default violation message.

name.description:
What the rule is called, used to report it (`body.content.rules.<name>`).
Optional: an unnamed rule reports by its position instead
(`body.content.rules[0]`). Two rules in this array sharing a name is a
config error naming both.

path.description: Path through the heading tree selecting the section(s) to assert over.

when.description: Optional filter expression gating this rule to matching tasks only.

DedupMode.description: `mt add`'s collision policy when the destination stem already exists: `fail` bails before writing, `skip` exits 0 without writing and reports the existing path, `add-suffix` mints `-2`, `-3`, … until a free stem turns up. `mt add --dedup` overrides this for one run; see `[tasks.naming] dedup` for the unset default.

max.description: The most matches of `pattern` a single unit may carry.

pattern.description: Rust regex counted within each unit.

per.description: Unit granularity the density is measured over. Defaults to `section`.

DensityUnit.description: Unit granularity a `density` content assert is measured over. Defaults to `section`.

breadcrumb-root.description: Fold the root name into the breadcrumb chain (`mt`, `mt:backend`, …).

collect.description: Active collectors; both may run at once (union, dedupe).

enabled.description: Default derivation switch for roots that set no `derive-tags` of their own.

slugify.description: Normalise folder names to tag form.

anyOf.description: Enable or disable for every file under the root.
Enable only for files matching this glob.
Enable only for files matching any of these globs.

DeriveTags.description:
Per-root derivation switch: a bool, a single file glob, or a list of globs.
A glob gates which files under the root get derivation (matched against the
path relative to the root). `true`/`false` enable or disable wholesale.

DictCase.description: How a compiled dictionary compares a lookup against its entries.

oneOf.description:
ASCII-case-insensitive: a capitalised title word matches a lowercase
entry. The default.
Byte equality.

DictSpec.description: `[dicts.<name>]` — one named string set, as declared in config.

case.description:
How a lookup compares against the entries: `fold` (the default) is
ASCII-case-insensitive, `exact` is byte equality.

include.description:
Other dictionaries — project or built-in — whose entries are unioned in.
The entries arrive raw; this dict's own `case` decides how they compare.

path.description:
A file of entries, one per line, relative to the project root. Blank
lines and lines whose first non-blank character is `#` are skipped, and
each entry is trimmed. May leave the root (`../shared/verbs.txt`), the
same rule `[[typst.local-packages]] path` follows.

DriftConfig.description:
`[tasks.estimate.drift]` — how `mt check` compares the working tree against
the budget the in-flight tasks declare.

Inert until some in-flight task actually declares an estimate in `unit`, so
a project that never uses a file budget never sees the check.

exclude.description:
Glob patterns naming paths the file count never counts — generated
output nobody hand-edits, so touching it should never cost part of a
budget spent on the source that produced it. Matched against the path
git reports, repo-root-relative (the same root `mt` runs against, not
the task root), with the same glob syntax as `[tasks.roots]
derive-tags`: `*` matches within one path segment, `**` crosses
directory boundaries. Empty = nothing excluded.

in-flight.description:
Filter expression naming the tasks in flight. The working tree carries
one diff and nothing in it says which file belongs to which task, so this
is what attribution rests on. Default `status == "wip"`.

line-multiple.description:
Lines allowed per declared file before the secondary soft line warning.
`0` disables it. Default 200.

message.description: Replaces the default advice in a drift report.

unit.description: Estimate unit read as the file budget. Default `files`.

EstimateBound.description:
One `[[tasks.estimate.max]]` / `[[tasks.estimate.min]]` entry: per-unit
quantities, gated by `when` and explained by `message`.

message.description:
Why the bound sits where it does; replaces the default advice in a
breach report.

when.description:
Filter expression selecting the tasks this entry bounds. Absent means
every task.

EstimateConfig.description: `[tasks.estimate]` — estimate units, bounds, and drift policy.

max.description:
Upper bounds (`[[tasks.estimate.max]] files = 5`), first matching entry
per unit wins. A unit no matching entry names is unbounded above. A
single table is accepted as one unconditional entry.

min.description:
Lower bounds (`[[tasks.estimate.min]] files = 1`), resolved like `max`.
A unit no matching entry names is unbounded below.

required.description: Whether an estimate must be set.

units.description: Allowed unit names. Empty = any unit.

FieldConfig.description: `[tasks.fields.<name>]` — constraints for one configurable core field.

default.description: Default value (informational; not auto-applied during load).

required.description: Whether the field must be set.

values.description:
Allowed enum values. Empty = any. An entry of the form `@<dict>`
expands to that `[dicts.<name>]` set at config load, so this list may
mix literal values and dictionary references, unioned in order — see
[`expand_dict_refs`].

FlipAction.description:
One action of a `[[on.flip]]` entry.

Exactly one of `show`, `list`, or `run` must be set, OR `gate = true` with
no `run` at all — the three kinds share one flat TOML shape so a mistyped
or conflicting entry surfaces as a clear config error instead of an opaque
parse failure.

gate.description:
Whether a non-zero exit from `run` refuses the flip, or — with no `run`
at all — refuses unconditionally. `run`-only (or run-less-gate-only).

list.description: `{ list = "filter or @view" }` — print the matching tasks.

message.description:
Explanation printed when a `run` command exits non-zero, or a run-less
gate refuses.

run.description:
`{ run = "command" }` — execute a command through the platform shell
(`sh -c`; `cmd /C` on Windows). Optional on a gating action: `gate =
true` with no `run` refuses the flip unconditionally whenever `when`
matches, with no command to run.

FlipHook.description: One `[[on.flip]]` entry: which transitions it fires on, and what it does.

actions.description: Actions to run, in declaration order.

when.description:
Filter over the task being flipped, plus `into("status")` for the status
being stamped. Empty fires on every flip.

FormatConfig.description: `[format]` — how `mt` canonicalizes task source before writing it.

enabled.description:
Run typstyle over the Typst source `mt` writes (`add`, `flip`, `review`,
`recur`, `import`), so surgical edits and slot fills land in one canonical
shape. `true` by default; set `false` to keep writes as raw byte splices
(minimal diffs, at the cost of drift like stray body indentation).

Framework.description:
One framework definition: typed inputs plus either a scalar score formula or
a categorical classification.

inputs.description: Declared inputs, keyed by name (the names used in formulas/predicates).

score.description: Scalar score formula (evalexpr). Mutually exclusive with `categories`.

HandleConfig.description: `[handle]` — the shape of a `mt ls` handle.

check-len.description:
How many check characters follow a handle's ordinal; omitted → 1.
A handle of any other length is refused rather than prefix-matched, so
raising this invalidates the short handles rather than accepting them.

HeaderAction.description: The shape of a body-header rule.

HeaderPathSegment.description: One step in a heading path: an exact string (direct-child match) or `{ match = "regex", recursive = bool }`.

match.description: Rust regex matched against heading text.

recursive.description: Match any descendant (true) or only direct children (false).

HeaderRuleConfig.description:
One entry in `[[tasks.body.headers.rules]]`.

`action` selects the rule shape and which fields apply:
- `require` / `forbid` / `unique` — cardinality over `path`.
- `order` — `before` headings must precede `after` headings.
- `allowlist` — closed-world: under `scope` (or top-level when omitted), only
  `allowed` headings are permitted.

action.description:
Whether the target headings must exist, must not, or must be unique, or
whether this is an `order`/`allowlist` rule.

after.description: Path whose headings must come after (`order`).

before.description: Path whose headings must come first (`order`).

message.description: Override for the default violation message.

name.description:
What the rule is called, used to report it (`body.headers.rules.<name>`).
Optional: an unnamed rule reports by its position instead
(`body.headers.rules[0]`). Two rules in this array sharing a name is a
config error naming both.

path.description: Path through the heading tree (cardinality actions).

scope.description:
Path selecting scopes whose children are constrained (`allowlist`);
omit to constrain top-level headings.

when.description: Optional filter expression gating this rule to matching tasks only.

rules.description: Ordered list of heading gating rules.

HyperlinkChoice.description:
`[ls] hyperlinks` — whether the `#` and `file` columns' cells carry an
OSC 8 hyperlink sequence (`ESC ] 8 ; ; <uri> ST <text> ESC ] 8 ; ; ST`) in
a standalone terminal, both pointing at the same per-row target. The `mt`
binary's `--hyperlinks` flag is this same choice, mirrored one-to-one in
the CLI crate (which alone depends on `clap`) as
`crate::render::link::HyperlinkChoice` there.

There is no terminal capability query for OSC 8 support, so `auto` is a
heuristic (stdout is a TTY and `TERM` is not `dumb`), never a detection —
and unlike colour, which degrades to nothing on a terminal that ignores
it, an unsupported terminal can render the OSC 8 payload as visible
garbage. That asymmetry is why the default is `never`, not `auto`
(`truth/tasks/hyperlink-the-file-column-with-osc-8.typ`).

oneOf.description: Enable hyperlinks only when stdout is a TTY and `TERM` is not `dumb`.
Always emit OSC 8 hyperlink sequences.
Never emit hyperlink sequences.

format.description: Format requirement for an explicit `id:`. Default accepts any non-empty string.

IdFormat.description: Format requirement for an explicit task `id:` field.

Input.description: One declared input: its type and bounds (numbers) or allowed values (enums).

InputKind.description: The type of a framework input.

oneOf.description: A bounded number.
A boolean.
A string from a fixed set of values.

InteractiveMode.description: When `mt add` opens the interactive editor.

oneOf.description: Open in a terminal when a required slot is still unfilled (default).
Always open in a terminal; error when stdin/stdout is not a TTY.
Never open; behave as the non-interactive pipeline.

Legend.description:
The status legend: an ordered, displayable vocabulary.

Each entry binds a value to optional display attributes (glyph, colour,
label) plus the `terminal` flag. The legend defines the legal status
values, their lifecycle order, and how each renders. An empty legend is
unconstrained, though omitting `[[tasks.status]]` entirely still inherits
`MindTape`'s shipped six-value legend.

LegendEntry.description: One `[[tasks.status]]` entry: a value plus its display attributes.

color.description: Optional colour: a named ANSI colour or `#RRGGBB`.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `value`.

note.description:
Note requirement for a task landing in this status: whether the change
must (`required`), may (`optional`, the default), or must not
(`forbidden`) carry a note. Set per status rather than legend-wide, so
a project can demand a note for statuses with no automated check (e.g.
`blocked`, `failed`) while leaving others unconstrained.

terminal.description: Whether this value ends a task; required fields relax once terminal.

to.description:
Allowed next statuses when leaving this one — the outgoing edges of the
transition graph. Empty on every entry keeps the legend any-to-any
(unconstrained). Once any entry declares `to`, transitions are enforced
and an empty `to` marks a sink: nothing out but a same-status re-stamp.
A reopen edge is just a terminal (or any) state naming its target here.

value.description: The value this entry describes (e.g. a status name).

LimitSpec.description:
`[[tasks.limits]]` — one cap on a filter-matched set of tasks.

`filter` and `max` are required: a limit with no cap is not a limit, and
defaulting a missing `max` to zero would silently forbid the set outright.

filter.description:
Filter expression selecting the capped set. The `mt ls` filter language,
so `@name` / `in_view("name")` caps a named view and no second spelling
of "which tasks" is needed.

max.description: How many matching tasks are allowed at once; a greater count is a breach.

message.description: Replaces the default advice in the breach report.

severity.description: Whether a breach fails `mt check` or only warns. Default `warn`.

acyclic.description:
Whether edges of this kind must stay acyclic. Ignored unless `validate`
is `local-task-path` — there is no cycle without a task-graph edge.

blocking.description:
Whether edges of this kind gate readiness. Ignored unless `validate` is
`local-task-path` — a target outside the backlog is not a task to wait on.

name.description: Kind name, matched against an edge's `kind`.

note.description: Note requirement for edges of this kind.

regex.description:
Pattern for `validate = "regex"`: required for that validator, and
rejected for every other one. A missing or uncompilable pattern is a
config error, never a silently permissive kind.

validate.description:
What shape this kind's targets take. Defaults to `local-task-path`,
which is exactly the historical behaviour (a stem resolved against the
loaded tasks); any other value declares the targets to be artifacts
outside the backlog — a commit, a pull request, a build.

kinds.description: User-declared custom edge kinds, layered over the immutable built-ins.

path.description: Lib directory holding the package's `typst.toml`, relative to the root.

columns.description:
Per-column display settings, keyed by column name. The embedded floor
lists every column in [`LS_COLUMNS`], so an entry missing here is one a
config layer deleted — and a column with no `when` never renders.

columns-order.description:
Explicit column order and selection: when set, only the listed
columns render, in that order. Empty (the default) keeps the built-in
column set and order.

contains-fields.description:
Default `contains()` haystack when a call names no field: an ordered
list of field names drawn from `crate::fields::is_contains_field`'s
vocabulary (every `crate::fields::FIELDS` name, plus the text-only
tier `body`/`note`/`tags`). Empty (the default) keeps the shipped
sweep — `title`, `id`, `body` — unchanged; a project states its own
answer to widen it (e.g. to include `note`, the `links[].note` prose,
or `tags`) or narrow it. An explicitly named field in a `contains()`
call (`contains("x", note)`) always works regardless of this default.
Validated at config load
([`deserialize_contains_fields`]): an unknown name is a config error
naming the field and listing the valid set, never a silent drop.

date-format.description:
Global date display format applied to every rendered date column.
Tokens (longest-match-first): `YYYY` 4-digit year, `YY` 2-digit year,
`MMMM` full month name, `MMM` abbreviated month, `MM` zero-padded month,
`M` bare month, `DD` zero-padded day, `D` bare day.
Non-token characters pass through literally.
Default `None` renders ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`.

default-sort.description:
Default sort chain for `mt ls` when the caller passes no `--sort`.
Same spec grammar as `--sort`: `"field"` or `"field:asc"` / `"field:desc"`.
Validated at config load. When absent the shipped built-in chain applies.

default-view.description:
Name of the view that drives the default `mt ls` listing when the
caller passes no filter: falls back to the `[views.default]` view when
this is unset, or matches every task when neither is declared.
Validated at config load.

hyperlink-target.description:
Template for the shared per-row hyperlink target URI both `#` and
`file` link to: `{abs}` (the absolute path, the project root joined
with the task's `file`) and `{rel}` (the same working-directory-relative
path the `file` column displays) are substituted. Defaults to
`file://{abs}`; point it at another scheme (e.g. an editor's own URI
handler) to open elsewhere.

hyperlinks.description:
Hyperlink output for the `#` and `file` columns' cells: `auto`,
`always`, or `never` (the default). Mirrors `--hyperlinks`, which wins
over this key when passed — see [`HyperlinkChoice`] for what each
value means and why the default is not `auto`.

overdue-color.description: Colour for the overdue due-date accent. Defaults to `"red"`.

ready.description:
Display settings (glyph, colour, label) for the ready and blocked
states shown in the READY column. Defaults to `MindTape`'s built-in
values, so leaving this unset keeps the current behaviour.

rules.description:
Ordered auto-activation rules applied to a bare `mt ls` (no CLI
filter, no `@view`): the first rule whose condition holds (or that
has none) wins and supplies its filter, sort, and columns.

LsRule.description:
One `[[ls.rules]]` entry.

The first rule (top to bottom) whose `condition` holds — or that omits
`condition` entirely — drives the default `mt ls` listing. Its effective
facets are `import-views` composed left-to-right (per-facet last-wins),
then any manual `filter` / `sort` / `columns` override (highest
precedence). All fields are optional; a rule with none of them still
matches (by an absent `condition`) but contributes no facets.

columns.description:
Manual column list — highest precedence for the columns facet. An
entry may reference a view's columns with `@view`.

condition.description:
Condition expression over environment predicates such as
`on_branch`, `env`, `weekday`, and `now`. Absent means the rule always
matches.

filter.description:
Manual filter override — highest precedence for the filter facet.
Same grammar as `[views]`; may use `@view` / `in_view`.

import-views.description:
Ordered list of views to import facets from, composed left-to-right
(later entries win on conflict). Each entry is a view name (`"view"`,
importing its filter, sort, and columns) or a scoped form
(`"view(filter, sort)"`) naming just the facets to import.

name.description:
Shown in the trailer and the JSON envelope's `applied.rule`; falls
back to the condition text when unset.

sort.description:
Manual sort override — highest precedence for the sort facet. Same
spec grammar as `--sort`; an entry may splice `@view`.

NamingConfig.description:
`[tasks.naming]` — how `mt add`/`mt recur` mint a new task's filename stem,
and (`dedup`) what `mt add` does when the minted stem collides.

dedup.description:
Collision policy for `mt add`; `--dedup` overrides for one run. Unset
takes its default from `stem` — see [`NamingConfig::effective_dedup`].

stem.description: Stem template with macros. Unset ⇒ bare `{slug}` (today's behaviour).

NoteRule.description: Note requirement for an edge kind.

oneOf.description: A non-empty note is mandatory (the `related` escape hatch).
A note is allowed but not required (the default).
A note is rejected.

NumericField.description:
A numeric scalar field: a `[min, max]` scale plus, optionally, one
classification style — contiguous bands or labelled anchor points.
Defaults to an integer `0..9` scale with no classification.

kind.description: Whether the scale is integer or real.

required.description: Whether the field must be set.

OnConfig.description: `[on]` — hooks keyed by the event that fires them.

PriorityConfig.description:
`[tasks.priority]` — the priority numeric field plus its scoring frameworks.

Carries the same scale and band/anchor classification as `difficulty`, plus
framework selection on top. When `framework` names an active framework, a
task's priority is computed from that framework's inputs instead of a
hand-set integer; `allow-manual` decides whether a raw integer is still
accepted as an escape hatch. The `frameworks` table holds the built-in
frameworks deep-merged with any user-declared ones.

allow-manual.description: Whether a raw integer is accepted while a framework is active.

framework.description: Active framework name, matched against `frameworks`. `None` = raw numeric.

frameworks.description: Framework registry: built-ins deep-merged with user definitions.

kind.description: Whether the scale is integer or real.

required.description: Whether the field must be set.

code.description: Short project qualifier. Falls back to the root directory name when absent.

ReadyConfig.description:
`[ls.ready]` — the READY column's per-state display (glyph, colour, label).

One block covering both `ready` and `blocked` states (rather than nesting
under `[ls.columns.ready]`, which only carries a generic `when`): `blocked`
needs display attributes `ColumnConfig` has no room for. Every
field is optional so an omitted key falls back to the embedded floor's
value (or, absent even that, the renderer's own literal fallback).

blocked-color.description: Colour for the blocked state: a named ANSI colour or `#RRGGBB`.

blocked-glyph.description: Glyph shown for a blocked task.

blocked-label.description: Display label for the blocked state.

ready-color.description: Colour for the ready state: a named ANSI colour or `#RRGGBB`.

ready-glyph.description: Glyph shown for a ready (unblocked, non-terminal) task.

ready-label.description: Display label for the ready state.

RecurConfig.description: `[tasks.recur]` — the recurring-tasks feature gate and policy floor.

default-anchor.description: Anchor used when a task's `recur` omits one.

enabled.description:
Whether the recurrence feature is enabled. `false` rejects any
authored `recur` field outright, at both `mt check` and `mt recur`.

materialize.description: Materialize model used when a task's `recur` omits one.

max-advance.description: Runaway cap: `mt recur --advance N` refuses `N` above this.

rrule.description:
Whether the `rrule(...)` escape hatch is accepted. Off by default;
also requires `MindTape` to be built with the `rrule` cargo feature —
missing either gate rejects an authored `rrule(...)` with a clear
error message.

Requirement.description: Whether a field is required: `false` (never), `true` (always), or a filter expression matching exactly the tasks that must carry it (e.g. `"!terminal"` — required until the task reaches a terminal status).

RetireConfig.description: `[retire]` — the gitless `rm` tombstone: keep the file, flip the status terminal.

rename.description: Move the retired task file into a sibling folder of this name (e.g. `.archive`), omitted → file stays.

status.description: The terminal status the retired task flips to; defaults to the legend's first terminal status (an error if the legend declares none).

default-filter.description:
Filter selecting which tasks a bare `mt rm` (no target given) retires.
Defaults to `"terminal"`, sweeping every task in a terminal status.
An explicit ref or filter argument on the command line overrides it.

strategy.description: How inbound references to removed task(s) are handled; defaults to `"git-tombstone"` in a git repository, `"reject"` without one.

RmStrategy.description: How `rm` handles inbound references when the git-pinned SWHID tombstone rewrite is unavailable.

oneOf.description: Mint a git-pinned SWHID tombstone and rewrite inbound edges onto it (the default in a git repo).
Keep the task file, flip it to a terminal status — a tombstone without git.
Strip each inbound edge from the surviving tasks, then delete.
Refuse, listing every surviving task that references a removed task.

Role.description:
`[[roles]]` — one role name an actor can hold. Identity-only: the role
carries no payload; a reader's harness keys its own config by role name.

RootConfig.description: The table form of a task root.

name.description: Tag emitted for the root itself. Defaults to the path's last segment.

path.description: Directory (relative to the project root) holding one task per file.

RootSpec.description:
One `[[tasks.roots]]` entry: a bare path string, or a table with a display
name and per-root derivation rule. Both spellings coexist; `roots =
["tasks"]` and `[[tasks.roots]]` deserialize to the same `Vec<RootSpec>`.

RuleSpec.description:
`[[tasks.rules]]` — one assertion or check every selected task must
satisfy.

Exactly one of `assertion`/`check` is set on a rule that came through
[`crate::config::load_config`] — [`validate_rules`] refuses both or
neither at config load — but a hand-built `RuleSpec` (a test, or
`parse_config` alone) can carry either combination, so
[`CompiledRule::compile`] still treats it as a fact to check rather than an
invariant to assume.

assert.description:
Filter expression that must evaluate true for every task the rule
applies to. Exactly one of this and `check` is set.

check.description:
A Typst function to call instead of an `assert` expression. Exactly
one of this and `assertion` is set.

message.description:
What an `assert` breach tells the author to do, in place of the
default advice naming the `assert` expression itself. Has no effect on
a `check` rule: each string the function returns is already the
specific thing to fix.

name.description:
What the rule is called, used to report it (`rules.<name>`). Optional:
an unnamed rule reports by its position instead (`rules[0]`).

severity.description: Whether a breach fails the command or only reports. Default `warn`.

when.description:
Filter expression gating which tasks the rule applies to. Absent means
every task.

ScaleKind.description: Whether the scale carries integers or reals.

oneOf.description: Whole numbers; bands are inclusive and contiguous.
Real numbers; bands are half-open, the last one closed.

Severity.description: How a breached config-declared constraint reports.

oneOf.description: Print the breach; the command still succeeds. The default.
Print the breach and fail the command.

allowed.description:
Allowed tag names. Empty = any. An entry of the form `@<dict>`
expands to that `[dicts.<name>]` set at config load — see
[`FieldConfig::values`] and [`expand_dict_refs`].

TargetValidator.description:
What shape a link kind's targets take — the `validate` key of
`[[tasks.links.kinds]]`.

oneOf.description:
A filename stem resolved against the loaded task set (the default, and
the only validator whose edges join the task graph).
An RFC 3986 URI: a scheme, then only URI-legal characters.

A hexadecimal git object name, 7 to 64 characters — abbreviated SHA-1
through full SHA-256.
A UUID, in any of the forms the `uuid` crate parses.
A project-supplied pattern, taken from the kind's sibling `regex` key.
Anything non-empty — the deliberate opt-out.

TasksConfig.description: `[tasks]` — where tasks live and how they are constrained.

comments.description: Review-comment policy over a task's whole source file (`mt check`).

difficulty.description: Difficulty as a numeric-field instance (scale + anchor classification).

fields.description:
Constraints for the remaining configurable enum core fields, keyed by
Typst slot name (`kind`).

limits.description:
Work-in-progress caps: how many tasks may match a filter at once
(`[[tasks.limits]]`, enforced by `mt check`).

naming.description:
Task stem naming template (`mt add`/`mt recur` minting) and `mt add`'s
default collision policy (`dedup`).

priority.description:
Priority as a numeric-field instance (scale + band classification),
optionally driven by a configured scoring framework.

recur.description: Recurring-tasks feature gate and policy floor (`mt recur`).

roots.description: Directories (relative to the project root) holding one task per file.

rules.description:
Project-declared assertions every selected task must satisfy
(`[[tasks.rules]]`, enforced by the validation pass — so by `mt check`
and by every write command before it writes).

status.description:
Status legend: legal values in lifecycle order, plus per-value display
(glyph, colour, label) and the `terminal` flag.

default.description: Template stem `mt add` uses when none is named.

dirs.description: Dirs (relative to the project root) holding `*.typ` task templates.

local-packages.description:
Extra `@local/<name>` package overrides, each resolved from an in-tree
path so a worktree resolves a foreign package without a global install.
`MindTape`'s own `@local/mindtape` is auto-registered when `<root>/lib` is
the `mindtape` package; this seam covers any other package (e.g. a
consumer's own lib referenced by an `x-<ns>` extras helper).

columns.description:
Column set applied when this view drives columns (bundle mode or
`--columns @name`). Empty means the default column set.

filter.description:
Filter expression (the filter facet). May reference other views via
`in_view("other")` or the `@other` sugar. Empty means match-all.

sort.description:
Sort chain applied when this view drives sort (bundle mode or
`--sort @name`). Same spec grammar as `--sort`; empty means the default
order.

description: Schema for `.mindtape/config.toml`, MindTape's per-project configuration. MindTape is a white-list: every section is optional and inherits the shipped floor when omitted.

actors.description:
The project's actor registry (`[[actors]]`): named workers (people and
language models) that `assignee:` values may reference.

dicts.description:
Named string sets (`[dicts.<name>]`), so a vocabulary two rules share is
one list rather than two that drift. Each unions `values`, `path` and
`include` into one set, compiled and checked once at config load. The
`mindtape-` prefix is reserved for the built-in dictionaries.

format.description: Whether `mt` reformats the Typst source it writes (`[format]`).

handle.description: `[handle]` — how many check characters a `mt ls` handle carries.

on.description: Status-transition hooks (`[[on.flip]]`), run only by `mt flip`.

roles.description:
Declared role names (`[[roles]]`) actors may hold. Identity-only: a
role carries no payload; the reader's harness keys its own config by
role name by convention.

tasks.description: Task discovery, status lifecycle, and field constraints.

title: MindTape project configuration
